topics.name: Verbal Bullying
topics.definition: Verbal bullying involves hurtful words or spoken behavior used repeatedly to upset, threaten, or humiliate someone.
examples: Repeated name-calling or mocking a classmate.
Teasing someone about their body, family, or background.
topics.signs: Repeated insults, name-calling, mocking, hurtful teasing, or threats that target a person.
effects: Losing confidence or avoiding class participation.
topics.prevention: Use respectful language, think before speaking, and speak up safely when words are being used to hurt someone.
topics.responses: Do not join in or laugh along. If it is safe, show support and tell a trusted adult about what happened.
seekHelp: Tell a trusted adult such as your class adviser or the Guidance Office.
Keep a record of what happened if the behavior continues.

topics.name: Physical Bullying
topics.definition: Physical bullying uses physical actions to hurt, intimidate, or frighten another person.
examples: Blocking or trapping someone to frighten them.
topics.signs: Repeated hitting, pushing, kicking, damaging belongings, or physical intimidation.
effects: Fear of going to certain places at school.
Feeling unsafe or always on guard.
topics.prevention: Respect personal space and belongings. Report unsafe behavior and ask adults for help early.
topics.responses: Prioritize safety. Do not physically intervene if it could put you at risk; get help from a teacher or trusted adult immediately.
seekHelp: Move to a safe place and find a teacher or trusted adult immediately.
Report the incident even if you were not the one who was hurt.

topics.name: Cyberbullying
topics.definition: Cyberbullying is hurtful or threatening behavior using digital tools such as social media, messaging apps, games, or online posts.
examples: Sending repeated hurtful or threatening messages.
Posting embarrassing photos or videos without permission.
Excluding someone from group chats to hurt them.
topics.signs: Repeated hurtful messages, humiliating posts, targeted group chats, threats, or sharing private content without permission.
effects: Feeling anxious even at home because messages continue.
Feeling embarrassed or afraid to use social media.
topics.prevention: Pause before posting, protect personal information, use privacy tools, and never share content meant to embarrass another person.
topics.responses: Do not reply with more harm or forward the content. Save relevant evidence if safe, block or report the account, and tell a trusted adult.
seekHelp: Tell a trusted adult and save evidence if it is safe to do so.
Use the block and report tools of the app or platform.
Ask the school office for help if classmates are involved.

topics.name: Social/Relational Bullying
topics.definition: Social or relational bullying tries to harm someone's friendships, belonging, or reputation.
examples: Deliberately leaving someone out of group activities.
Spreading rumors to damage a classmate's reputation.
Pressuring others to stop being friends with someone.
topics.signs: Deliberately excluding a student to hurt them, spreading rumors, or pressuring a group to turn against someone.
effects: Feeling sad or withdrawn at school.
topics.prevention: Include others, check whether information is true before repeating it, and respect people's right to choose their friends.
topics.responses: Be welcoming without escalating the conflict. Do not spread rumors, and tell a trusted adult when it continues or causes harm.
seekHelp: Talk to a trusted adult about what you noticed.
Invite the person to join safe school activities.

topics.name: Psychological/Emotional Bullying
topics.cardText: Be kind to the mind and heart.
topics.definition: Psychological or emotional bullying involves repeated harmful behavior that makes a person feel afraid, ashamed, pressured, or isolated.
examples: Pressuring someone through threats or coercion.
Making someone feel worthless on purpose.
topics.signs: Repeated intimidation, humiliation, coercion, threats, or behavior intended to make someone feel worthless or unsafe.
topics.prevention: Treat people with dignity, respect boundaries, and take concerns seriously even when there are no visible injuries.
topics.responses: Listen without blaming the person. Encourage them to talk to a trusted adult and seek support if they feel worried or unsafe.
seekHelp: Tell a trusted adult; emotional harm is real harm.
Ask the Guidance Office about available support.
